Subject: Re: planned migration - temporary SLA request

Hi Sean —

Quick note from TrellisPay operations: we have a scheduled data-center migration window next week (Nov 3-5) that will temporarily alter our traffic patterns and increase the likelihood of support noise during the 02:00–06:00 PT window. Our internal runbook flags a potential for elevated P1/P2 alerts while backend IPs are rehomed.

Ask: can Redwood temporarily augment on-call coverage or accept a short-term adjustment to the P2 response SLA (from 4 hours to 8 hours) for incidents originating from the migration window? We are prepared to accept a reduced SLO for that window in exchange for a reduced credit burden.

We need to confirm by EOD Nov 1 so we can finalize our mutual action plan with procurement. If possible, we'd like a written confirmation of the proposed exception + a short list of escalation contacts.

Thanks,
Alex Chen

Subject: RE: Temporary on-call augmentation & P1/P2 response mitigation request - TrellisPay migration

Alex — thanks for the details. Short answer: yes, we can support a short-term mitigation plan. Longer answer below with proposed options and next steps.

Options we can offer (pick one or combine):
1) On-call augmentation: Redwood will temporarily add a dedicated responder rota (1 additional senior engineer) covering 02:00–06:00 PT for the migration nights. Cost: one-time augmentation fee plus hourly.
2) SLA alignment/waiver: Approve a temporary P2 response window of 8 hours for the three-night window (Nov 3–5) with no automatic credit; credits may be negotiated if we hit defined thresholds in the MAP.
3) Traffic-safety routing: Route TrellisPay production traffic to a higher-availability pool and enable prefetched KV-cache warming for the migration period. This will reduce incident surface but may increase token unit cost temporarily.

Immediate asks from TrellisPay to finalize:
- Confirm which option you prefer (augmentation vs waiver vs hybrid)
- Provide the migration runbook or a link to the runbook for our on-call engineers to review
- Approve the attached mutual action plan (I attached a draft MAP and a SLO-waiver template)

I've looped in Marcus (serving) for feasibility and Laura (support ops) for operational readiness and escalation contact prep. If you approve augmentation, we need to finalize by EOD Nov 1 to staff the rota.

Attachments: trellispay_mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf, slo-waiver-template.docx

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

I reviewed the runbook excerpt Alex pasted in the portal link. Quick technical notes:

- Augmentation: we can staff +1 senior on-call for the 02:00–06:00 PT window for Nov 3–5. That person will be configured with elevated paging and direct access to the TrellisPay routing group. We recommend pairing them with the normal overnight responder on day 1 to ensure handoff.
- Routing to HA pool: feasible but requires a rolling model restart to attach VMs to the higher-capacity pool; estimate 90–120 minutes of work outside the migration window to prepare. There will be a modest cost delta (~12% token unit cost increase) for the routed requests for the three nights.
- Monitoring: we'll create a temporary synthetic check (1-min frequency) and a dedicated Grafana dashboard; Ops will alert the on-call via pagerduty escalation policy 1->2->manager.

If TrellisPay selects augmentation + HA routing we should:
1) Execute the MAP (attached) and sign the SLO waiver for the three nights
2) Redwood to enable HA routing at 00:00 PT on Nov 3 and revert at 08:00 PT on Nov 5
3) On-call augmentation to be active nights Nov 3/4/5 with a single senior augmentation per night

Cost estimate in the MAP header (see attached) for the hybrid approach: augmentation fee $4,200 + estimated runtime delta $650/night.

I'll standby for Alex to confirm which option TrellisPay prefers; we can also do a hybrid where we waive P2 on night 1 and augment nights 2–3 to reduce cost.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
